EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the classic monosubstituted benzene Raman pattern: a very strong ring-breathing band at 1005 cm⁻¹ with the companion band at 1032 cm⁻¹, strong aromatic C–H stretch at 3064 cm⁻¹ (supported by GFQ-003), the ring C=C stretching doublet at 1606/1585 cm⁻¹, and characteristic out-of-plane/low-frequency aromatic modes near 771 and 624 cm⁻¹. The aliphatic C–H stretch multiplet (2879–3005 cm⁻¹) and CH deformation near 1446 cm⁻¹ indicate a small alkyl substituent (CH3/CH2) without heteroatom stretches (no OH/NH bands). This best fits ethylbenzene (candidate 1) over disubstituted or heteroatom-containing candidates.
